_comment: E2E (manual, live): Approach A. Agent generates an image via image_generation (returns document_id) then inserts it into an OPERATOR-PROVIDED Google Doc via gdocs_insert_image_after_text using attachment_id, IN THE SAME TURN. Replace <YOUR_DOC_ID>. Needs OPENAI_API_KEY + COLMENA_LOCAL storage + DATABASE_URL (the attachment registry is built from it) + OAuth creds in-memory + --agent-session-id. VERIFIED LIVE LOCAL (2026-06-20): same-turn generate->insert works thanks to the live AttachmentRegistry fallback in lookup_storage_key (CHANGELOG §45) — the generated image is registered to the registry and resolved live (snapshot miss -> registry hit). The gdocs path uses the Docs API (read_outline/insert), not Drive export, so a shared doc works.

test_payload.prompt:
Do these steps in order on Google Doc id <YOUR_DOC_ID>:
1. Call generate_image with prompt 'a simple flat-design red circle on a white background'. Note the document_id in the result.
2. Call gdocs_read_outline on <YOUR_DOC_ID> and pick a short exact text_preview substring from the first non-empty paragraph as your anchor. Do NOT call gdocs_read_as_markdown.
3. Call gdocs_insert_image_after_text with doc_id=<YOUR_DOC_ID>, anchor=<that substring>, attachment_id=<the document_id from step 1>. Do NOT pass image_url. Do NOT pass width_pt/height_pt.
4. Report the EXACT step-3 tool result verbatim: the changes array, revision_id_after, and any soft_warnings.

config.system_message: You are a document editor that can generate images and place them in a Google Doc. Use gdocs_read_outline (Docs API) to find anchors — never gdocs_read_as_markdown. The generate_image result returns a document_id; pass that exact value as the attachment_id argument. Report tool results verbatim.

generate_image.name: generate_image
generate_image.description: Generate a brand-new image from a text prompt. Returns an object containing a document_id for the generated image. Pass that document_id as attachment_id to gdocs_insert_image_after_text.

prompt.description: Detailed text prompt describing the image to generate.
